author: reek
body: A call to is-letter reaches one of two implementations, and the chapter's cite list decides which: a chapter citing Foreword chapter CCE resolves the chapter definition, and a chapter citing nothing reaches the compiler builtin (emit-is-letter-builtin). The two are one band-pair that must not drift apart, and the compiler reaches the predicate only through the CCE definition, so the builtin needs its own runner. This chapter therefore deliberately cites nothing.

author: reek
body: Because this chapter cites nothing it is also the only probe that can see the ARM64 and RISC-V plugs disagree with x86. A chapter that cites CCE answers from the chapter definition on every target and hides the whole divergence; run this one under build/test-cross.ps1 after touching either plug's is-char-class dispatch.
